recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as the FHIR-37373 reconciliation. If FHIR-I applies FHIR-51598 later, handle that as a separate wording update about chaining placement around :identifier, not as a change to the no-stacked-modifiers rule.
issue_request: FHIR-37373 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I clarification asking whether a reference type modifier, :identifier, and token :of-type could be combined in one reference search parameter such as Consent?consenter:Patient:identifier:of-type=.... The accepted resolution pointed to FHIR-20641 and stated that chained/stacked modifiers are not permitted.
initial_application: Commit fd19eba3ff735b49eb917ed3b722ce8511f8011f applied FHIR-37373 by adding the active source/search.html statement that only a single modifier is allowed on a single search parameter. Commit 1e3b7571675379e59420a5ceaba188bd20bb1012 applied the related FHIR-20641 guidance to define a new search parameter or operation when multiple layers of modification are needed.
additional_context: The seed Zulip thread contains the same consenter:Patient:identifier:of-type question and led to the Jira. FHIR-I minutes from 2022-05-23 confirm FHIR-37373 was accepted as Persuasive with Modification by pointing to FHIR-20641 because modifier chaining is prohibited. Later source work, including FHIR-50614, clarifies resource type modifier values such as subject:Patient, while FHIR-51598 is a separate Resolved - change required clarification about chaining before versus after :identifier and does not change the stacked-modifier prohibition.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The final combined branch source/search.html still states that the type modifier value is the resource type itself, immediately states that only one modifier is allowed on a single search parameter, and gives the FHIR-20641 alternative of defining a new search parameter or operation for layered behavior.
